subject: GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection - follow up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection - follow up

Hi Rebecca —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and next steps from our call: 

1) You asked for our standard DPA and guidance on which SCC module to use for ACME’s procurement process. I’ve attached the current DPA (Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf) and a short SCC selection matrix (SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx) to make the mapping easier.

2) SOC 2 status: Redwood completed a SOC 2 Type II (Security & Availability) in June 2025. We can share the attestation under NDA — let me know if you want the report sent or uploaded to your SSO portal.

3) Controller/Processor alignment: As discussed, Redwood generally acts as a data processor on behalf of our customers for hosted API usage. For some private deployments we provide features that allow customers to act as the controller; I summarize the roles in the attached DPA.

4) Vendor security questionnaire: you mentioned sending your questionnaire — we’re happy to fill it. Once you share it, I’ll loop in our security team and return a completed copy and any supporting evidence (SOC 2 summary, encryption diagrams, KMS info).

Next steps proposed: 
- Rebecca: please confirm whether your privacy/legal team prefers Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) based on the SCC matrix I attached.
- Marissa/Rishi/Laura: will prepare completed questionnaire + DPA redline if ACME prefers any edits.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v3.pdf, SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection - follow up

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. A couple of quick questions from our side: 

- We typically require the vendor to sign Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor) SCCs for SaaS/API relationships. Based on your note that Redwood is the processor, that aligns — can you confirm you are willing to execute Module 2?

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept our standard DPA redlines around data retention and subprocessor notification windows (I’ve pasted the key asks below)? If there are any clauses you can’t accept we can push via procurement.

- I’m attaching ACME’s vendor security questionnaire (ACME_vendor_security_questionnaire.docx) — if you can complete and return by end of week that would be great. Also please attach supporting evidence (SOC 2 summary, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM info).

Key asks (summary):
- Retention: ability to set retention to 90 days by default across logs and user data
- Subprocessor notice: 30-day advance notice and right to object
- Data deletion proof: API call or attestation within 14 days of request

If you can confirm Module 2 and send the completed questionnaire, procurement will move to the legal review phase.

Thanks —
Rebecca
Head of Privacy Operations | ACME Corp
rebecca.li@acme.com
(617) 555-0123

(Attachment: ACME_vendor_security_questionnaire.docx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-16 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: GDPR: DPA request & SCC module selection - follow up

Hi Rebecca —

Appreciate the clear asks. Confirming answers below and attaching our completed questionnaire: vendor_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf.

- SCC module: We can execute Module 2 (Controller-to-Processor). The SCC_selection_matrix.xlsx I sent maps our standard DPA to Module 2 language — happy to use that as the basis for DocuSign.

- Controller/Processor: Redwood will sign as Processor for hosted API and Dedicated instances where Redwood manages the inference runtime. The customer (ACME) will be Controller for personal data and will direct processing in the DPA. For Private/on-prem deployments where ACME fully controls the runtime and key management, we can discuss a Controller/Controller mapping but that’s outside the standard SaaS DPA — we flagged that in section 4 of the DPA.

- Retention: Our platform supports configurable retention; default logging retention is 90 days and longer-term retention can be configured per contract. We’re willing to include the 90-day default in the DPA.

- Subprocessor notice: We provide 30-day advance notice for new subprocessors and an objection right as part of the DPA notification process.

- Data deletion proof: We support programmatic data deletion and will provide an attestation within 14 days upon request; we’ll include the API call reference in the appendix of the DPA.

- SOC 2: As noted, we completed SOC 2 Type II (Security & Availability) in June 2025. I attached a redacted SOC 2 summary and the completed questionnaire. If you need the full report, we can arrange an NDA/secure upload.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll send the completed questionnaire (attached) and share a DocuSign DPA link once legal confirms the redline expectation.
- Rishi / Laura: I’m looping you for legal review / DPA signature authority.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_filled.pdf

Best,
Marissa
